stories.summary: La crisis que atraviesa la empresa ha abierto el debate sobre quién puede sustituir al hombre que lleva más de tres décadas tomando las grandes decisiones de la compañía

sources.title: ¿Quién podrá suceder a Jensen Huang como nuevo CEO de Nvidia? Los candidatos, sus trayectorias y a qué se dedican
sources.text: Nvidia se enfrenta a uno de los momentos más delicados de su historia. La compañía estadounidense, convertida en una pieza fundamental del desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial, se ha quedado sin el único consejero delegado que ha conocido desde su fundación en 1993. Las informaciones sobre las presuntas relaciones extramatrimoniales de Jensen Huang, una de ellas con una supuesta agente vinculada a China, han provocado una crisis que ha terminado con su salida. Según ha publicado The Wall Street Journal, la empresa estaba preparando su destitución, pero ha sido el consejo de administración quien, tras convocar una reunión extraordinaria para estudiar su futuro, ha terminado por dimitir. La situación ha adquirido una dimensión todavía mayor después de que The New York Times informase de una segunda relación extramatrimonial, esta vez con una ejecutiva de la propia compañía. Ahora que Huang ha tomado la decisión de salir, antes de que Nvidia confirmara oficialmente la destitución de Huang, la pregunta es clara: ¿quién dirigirá Nvidia sin Jensen Huang? Uno de los nombres que más fuerza ha cobrado es el de Colette Kress, vicepresidenta ejecutiva y directora financiera de Nvidia. Según recoge el Financial Times, fuentes próximas a la compañía consideran que sería la alternativa más sencilla para garantizar una transición ordenada si Huang abandona el cargo. Por el momento, es ella, precisamente, quien ha tomado el relevo de forma temporal. Kress llegó a Nvidia en septiembre de 2013 después de acumular una amplia experiencia en algunas de las principales empresas tecnológicas de Estados Unidos. Anteriormente, trabajó durante tres años en Cisco, donde fue responsable de la estrategia financiera, la planificación y el desarrollo de negocio de diferentes divisiones. También pasó 13 años en Microsoft, cuatro de ellos como directora financiera de su división de servidores y herramientas, y ocupó distintos puestos en Texas Instruments. Licenciada en Finanzas por la Universidad de Arizona y con un MBA por la Universidad Metodista del Sur, Kress conoce de primera mano las operaciones económicas de Nvidia y mantiene una relación estrecha con los inversores. Su experiencia gestionando las finanzas de grandes multinacionales tecnológicas podría resultar fundamental para tranquilizar a los mercados durante una posible transición. Sin embargo, su principal debilidad frente a otros candidatos es que no cuenta con una formación técnica comparable a la de Huang. Aunque domina las cuentas y la estrategia financiera, dirigir Nvidia también exige comprender una industria marcada por la innovación constante y la competencia por desarrollar los chips más avanzados. Si el consejo de administración apuesta por un perfil tecnológico, Ian Buck podría convertirse en uno de los principales aspirantes. El ingeniero se incorporó a Nvidia en 2004, después de completar su doctorado en Informática en la Universidad de Stanford, y actualmente ocupa el cargo de vicepresidente de computación a hiperescala y de alto rendimiento. Su trayectoria está estrechamente vinculada a uno de los mayores éxitos de Nvidia: CUDA, la plataforma que permite utilizar las tarjetas gráficas para realizar cálculos complejos y que hoy utilizan millones de desarrolladores, investigadores y científicos. Buck fue uno de sus principales impulsores y contribuyó a transformar las GPU en herramientas fundamentales para la inteligencia artificial. Actualmente, supervisa productos de hardware y software destinados a grandes clientes tecnológicos como Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Meta y OpenAI. Su trabajo consiste en colaborar con estas compañías para desarrollar e implementar soluciones de inteligencia artificial generativa, una de las áreas más importantes del negocio de Nvidia. Además, Buck cuenta con experiencia institucional. Ha comparecido ante el Congreso de Estados Unidos para abordar cuestiones relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial, ha asesorado a la Casa Blanca y ha participado en proyectos internacionales para desarrollar superordenadores destinados a la investigación científica. Su principal fortaleza es el profundo conocimiento técnico de los productos de Nvidia. Sin embargo, a diferencia de Kress, no pertenece al círculo más cercano de Huang, lo que podría dificultar su elección como sustituto inmediato. Entre las alternativas externas destaca Lisa Su, presidenta y consejera delegada de AMD, uno de los principales competidores de Nvidia. Su nombre resulta especialmente atractivo por su experiencia liderando la transformación de una empresa tecnológica y reforzando su posición en el mercado de los semiconductores. Su llegó a AMD en enero de 2012 como vicepresidenta sénior y directora general de sus unidades de negocio. Posteriormente, asumió la dirección de operaciones, desde donde impulsó la integración de diferentes departamentos y contribuyó a reorganizar la compañía. Su trayectoria anterior incluye puestos de responsabilidad en Freescale Semiconductor, IBM y Texas Instruments. A diferencia de otros posibles candidatos, Su combina una sólida formación técnica con experiencia empresarial y capacidad de gestión. Durante sus 13 años en IBM desempeñó diferentes funciones de ingeniería y dirección, incluida la vicepresidencia de su centro de investigación y desarrollo de semiconductores. Su liderazgo también ha recibido numerosos reconocimientos. En 2024 fue elegida consejera delegada del año por la revista TIME y en 2026 recibió la Medalla Nacional de Ciencias de Estados Unidos, uno de los principales reconocimientos científicos del país. Su posible incorporación a Nvidia, sin embargo, presenta un obstáculo evidente. Y es que actualmente dirige una de las compañías que compiten directamente con ella. Convencerla para abandonar AMD supondría una operación extraordinaria, aunque su experiencia gestionando grandes transformaciones empresariales la convierte en una de las figuras más preparadas para afrontar un relevo de estas características.

sources.title: Dimite Jensen Huang, CEO de Nvidia, tras el escándalo de sus infidelidades y su relación con una espía china
sources.text: El hombre más importante para la industria de la IA en estos momentos se marcha. Jensen Huang, CEO de Nvidia, ha presentado su renuncia. Una decisión que llega tras cuatro días en el ojo del huracán después de que la compañía anunciase que iba a investigar la relación extramatrimonial que mantuvo con una empresaria china cliente de la multinacional que, en realidad, sería una presunta agente de inteligencia de Pekín. Este final parece haberse precipitado horas después de que trascendiera un segundo affaire, en esta ocasión con una subordinada directa. La junta directiva mantuvo este miércoles un encuentro en el que se puso su despido sobre la mesa. Finalmente, no han tenido que obligar a Huang a marcharse, sino que ha decidido dimitir, tal y como ha adelantado la agencia Reuters. La polémica ha afectado y mucho al valor de la compañía, que hasta hace apenas diez días presumía de ser la empresa con mayor capitalización bursátil del mundo, puesto que recuperó Apple el pasado 3 de noviembre. En las últimas cinco sesiones, Nvidia ha perdido cerca de 470.000 millones de dólares. Algo que ha profundizado en una caída que se inició hace un mes, cuando ha visto esfumarse 1,33 billones de su valor. En cuatro semanas ha pasado de 5,52 billones de dólares de valor en Bolsa a 4,19 billones tras el cierre de los mercados este miércoles. Nada más abrir los mercados, sus títulos caían más de un 14%. Y es previsible que esa caída pueda acentuarse en los próximos días, porque su sucesión no es precisamente sencilla. De momento, Colette Kress , directora financiera, será la que asumirá de forma interina el rol de CEO. La junta ha asegurado que se pone en marcha para buscar un candidato para reemplazarle de forma definitiva, sondeando opciones tanto fuera como dentro de la compañía. Hasta que saltó el escándalo de la presunta trampa de miel tendida por una espía china (un extremo, por cierto, que Pekín niega), nadie había cuestionado públicamente el liderazgo hiperpersonalista que Jensen Huang ejecutaba sobre la organización. Durante más de 30 años, el tiempo que ha pasado desde que fundó la compañía en 1993, ha creado y mantenido una estructura en la que prácticamente todas las decisiones de negocio, fuesen del ámbito que fuesen, eran supervisadas por él. Él dirigía y controlaba a un grupo de sesenta ejecutivos que le reportaban diariamente. A diferencia de otras grandes tecnológicas, concentró todo el negocio en su figura. No hubo nunca un presidente ni un vicepresidente ejecutivo que estuviese llamado a reemplazarle. Esto no era sinónimo de que hubiese un plan a largo plazo. El propio Huang había colocado a sus hijos y su yerno en puestos de alta responsabilidad como si se tratase de una empresa familiar. Es cierto que el fundador era el máximo accionista (con un 4% de los títulos) pero estos nombramientos llamaron la atención en su momento porque ninguno de ellos tenía experiencia previa en el sector tecnológico. Su hija Madison se formó en pastelería y trabajó en el grupo LVMH. Spencer, por su parte, regentaba un bar en Taiwán. Sin embargo, su padre les empujó a estudiar en el MIT, así como cursar estudios superiores de administración de empresas. Su falta de experiencia en otras grandes tecnológicas no fue obstáculo para que se les adjudicasen sueldos millonarios y se les pusiera al frente de divisiónes como la de realidad virtual o robótica. Sin embargo, la tormenta en torno a las relaciones extramatrimoniales de su padre y el presunto espionaje de Pekín ha desbarato sus opciones para una sucesión familiar. sources.text: La compañía de inteligencia artificial Nvidia ha cobrado especial protagonismo durante los últimos días tras conocerse los escándalos que envuelven a su ya antiguo CEO. Jensen Huang , quien ha ocupado el cargo hasta hace escasas horas, ha dimitido tras revelarse dos infidelidades . Una de ellas con una presunta espía china y otra con una subordinada directa. Debido a este escándalo, la junta directiva de la empresa evaluó su posible despido , pero que no ha tenido que llevarse a cabo, ya que Huang presentó su renuncia voluntaria. Esta crisis ha impactado severamente en el mercado. En las últimas cinco sesiones, la multinacional ha perdido cerca de 470.000 millones de dólares de capitalización, profundizando una caída que alcanza los 1,32 billones en un mes. En bolsa, Nvidia ha pasado de valer 5,52 billones de dólares a 4,19 billones , cediendo a Apple el primer puesto mundial. La sucesión plantea dudas operativas debido al modelo hiperpersonalista de Huang, quien fundó la empresa en 1993 y supervisaba directamente a sesenta ejecutivos sin haber designado un relevo claro. Ante este vacío en el liderazgo, el cargo de Huang lo ocupará, de manera temporal, la vicepresidenta ejecutiva y directora financiera de la compañía, Colette Kress, quien se incorporó al puesto en septiembre de 2013 , avalada por casi 25 años de experiencia en grandes firmas tecnológicas, según consta en la página web de Nvidia. Antes de su llegada, Kress trabajó tres años en Cisco como vicepresidenta sénior y directora financiera del grupo BTOF. En esa división asumió la responsabilidad sobre la estrategia financiera, la planificación, la generación de informes y el desarrollo de todos los segmentos operativos y de ingeniería. Su trayectoria previa incluye trece años en Microsoft , donde ejerció durante cuatro ejercicios como directora financiera de la división de Servidores y Herramientas , además de ocupar diversos puestos de responsabilidad vinculados a la planificación. Sus inicios profesionales se desarrollaron en el área financiera de Texas Instruments. En el ámbito académico, la nueva máxima responsable de la multinacional tecnológica es graduada en Finanzas por la Universidad de Arizona . Asimismo, completó su formación superior cursando un máster en Administración de Empresas (MBA) impartido por la Universidad Metodista del Sur. Además, Forbes situó a Kress en el puesto número 32 en el ranking 2026 America's Richest Self-Made Women Net Worth (mujeres que se hicieron ricas a sí mismas), con un patrimonio de 1.200 millones de dólares. Según Reuters , al cierre del mercado este miércoles, sus acciones en Nvidia estaban valoradas en aproximadamente 750 millones de dólares. sources.title: Jensen Huang built Nvidia into a $4 trillion AI giant but owned less than 4% of it, leaving him without the super-voting power to protect his CEO role
sources.text: Jensen Huang, the billionaire ex- Nvidia CEO who took the company from a small player in the video game graphics industry to the chipmaker at the center of the AI revolution, once made a surprising revelation: He could be fired at any time. “In a well-governed company, the CEO was always designed to report to the board of directors and the board of directors report to shareholders,” Huang said in a January podcast interview with Jodi Shelton. “If the CEO doesn’t do his job according to 12, 13, 15 board members, however sized the board is, that CEO is let go.” This reality sets Nvidia apart from other Silicon Valley companies, especially those still run by a cofounder. That includes Meta , where CEO and cofounder Mark Zuckerberg wields considerable power over the board due to its dual class share structure. On Thursday, Huang resigned from the company that he cofounded and led over the past 33 years after publicly admitting to being unfaithful to his wife. Nvidia’s board opened an independent investigation into Huang and the possibility he may have been a target of a foreign intelligence operation after reporting by the New York Times explored his close relationship with a businesswoman that U.S. intelligence identified as a Chinese spy. Huang reportedly had another affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him, according to the New York Times . On Thursday, the board appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. Still, Huang said in that January interview any future Nvidia CEO would not measure up to him. “There will never be one like me, and the reason for that is because I was raised by the company,” he said at the time. Nvidia did not immediately respond to Fortune ’s request for comment. Despite being the company’s largest individual shareholder, Huang did not have unparalleled voting control over his company or outsized control over the company’s board, like other founders. Huang owned about 870.6 million Nvidia shares, or about 3.58% of the company as of March, according to the company’s 2026 proxy statement. His holdings were far greater than that of other executives and directors, including Kress, who held 4.4 million shares. Vanguard and BlackRock both owned more than 7% of the company each. Because of Nvidia’s one-share-one vote system, Huang’s stake doesn’t come with special privileges, despite his status as a cofounder. That means the number of votes he has directly corresponds with his number of shares. As Huang alluded to in his January podcast interview, Nvidia’s bylaws are written in such a way that the company’s CEO can be removed by the board for any reason and at any time—still, Huang lacked enough voting power to independently elect or remove Nvidia’s directors. While founders with majority voting control, such as Zuckerberg, can effectively determine who sits on their boards, Huang would have needed support from other Nvidia shareholders to do the same. That differs from other companies run by tech founders including Meta, Snap , and even Google. At Meta, a dual class voting structure (it said last month it would add a third non-voting tier next year ) gives Zuckerberg outsized power over voting. Despite owning 13.4% of the company, Zuckerberg controls about 60% of the company’s voting power because his class B shares give him 10 votes each compared to one vote for every class A share. With this voting power, Zuckerberg can effectively elect Meta’s entire board and is the deciding voice on most matters sent to shareholders. Snap, the social media company, has a similar arrangement with CEO and cofounder Evan Spiegel controlling 53% of the company’s voting power while only owning about 9.3% of the company. Even at Google parent company Alphabet , where cofounder Sergey Brin and cofounder and former CEO Larry Page no longer run day-to-day operations, the pair still collectively retain majority voting control of the tech giant. Both still serve on the company’s board. Nvidia’s stock plummeted by as much as 14% Thursday following the announcement of Huang’s departure, before rebounding. It was down about 4.7% as of 1:30 p.m. EST on Thursday. With a nearly $4 trillion market cap, the company makes up about 6% of the S&P 500 and about 10% of the Nasdaq 100 , meaning any reckoning it experiences will trickle through the broader market and everyday Americans’ 401(K) accounts. Huang was key to Nvidia’s operations with a flat management structure and direct involvement in the company’s product strategy and its supplier and customer relationships. In recent months, he has also cultivated a close relationship with President Donald Trump, who has been a vocal proponent of boosting the AI industry and the infrastructure backing it in the U.S.—although Trump was quick to back ex-Apple CEO Tim Cook as Huang’s successor on Thursday. The board has now made changes to its own structure as well. It previously operated without a board chairman, opting instead to rely on lead independent director Stephen Neal to oversee management. On Thursday, it appointed Harvey C. Jones, a former semiconductor company CEO and Nvidia board member since 1993, as its chairman of the board, it said in a statement. Kress, the company’s CFO since 2013, said for her part she is planning to build on Huang’s legacy at Nvidia as interim CEO she said in a Thursday statement. In the January interview, Huang said while he didn’t love his job every day, he always tried his “mightiest” because of two reasons. “One, I’m the best person for the job. I believe that,” he said. “And, two, I have to earn being the best person for that job every day.”

sources.title: Nvidia’s next CEO: The outside contenders to succeed Jensen Huang
sources.text: The biggest guessing game in business has begun: Who can fill Jensen Huang’s shoes? Colette Kress, chief financial officer at Nvidia since 2013, was appointed interim CEO of the company on Thursday. Kress will also continue in her CFO role as the board conducts its search for Jensen Huang’s permanent successor. “Colette is very much the right interim CEO,” Scott W. Simmons, co-managing partner of executive search firm Crist Kolder Associates, told Fortune . But Simmons, who has worked in executive recruiting for almost 30 years, thinks Nvidia’s board will seek a technologist as Huang’s permanent successor, potentially from outside the company. If Nvidia goes with an external candidate for the CEO job, Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at The Futurum Group, is putting his money on Arm CEO Rene Haas. “He spent seven years at Nvidia and understands Jensen’s culture; and what makes him interesting is that Nvidia’s Grace and Vera CPUs run on Arm architecture,” Boloor wrote in an X post . “So while he missed [the] rise of NVLink, Mellanox and rack-scale AI he understands [the] CPU side of Nvidia’s platform better than almost anyone else on the outside.” Sam Sugarman, a venture capital and private equity investor who co-founded and leads the VC/PE Secondaries practice at Concordia Capital, also placed Haas on his list of external candidates . Haas would bring a combination of Nvidia experience and public-company leadership, having steered Arm through its 2023 IPO and expanded its business beyond processor licensing. His background spans engineering, product strategy and sales. But his familiarity with Nvidia dates to an earlier era: he left in 2013. The board will have to assess whether running Arm has prepared him for Nvidia’s much larger, more complex business. Sugarman also pointed to AMD CEO Lisa Su as a potential successor to Huang. Su (who ironically happens to be a distant cousin of Huang’s) would bring a combination of semiconductor engineering credentials and a proven record of running a major chipmaker. She has led AMD since 2014, overseeing a turnaround that made it a formidable competitor in processors and a challenger to Nvidia in AI chips. That experience could appeal to a board. But recruiting her would mean persuading a sitting CEO to leave the company she rebuilt. Meanwhile, Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at Yorkville Ives & Co., told Fortune that he sees Tim Cook , the former CEO of Apple ; Tom Kurian, CEO of Google Cloud; and Nikesh Arora, chairman and CEO of Palo Alto Networks , “as the top three external candidates for Nvidia’s CEO role.” Cook would bring experience with a challenge few executives have faced: succeeding a technology company’s defining leader. Cook took over from Steve Jobs and spent 15 years running Apple before becoming executive chairman in September. Cook’s mastery of supply chains and logistics would be a good fit at Nvidia, and the fact that Apple has developed its own processors in-house over the past decade means Cook has some direct experience in the chips business. His continuing work on Apple’s international relationships would also be relevant to a company navigating geopolitical pressures. But his continuing responsibilities at Apple as chairman could complicate the prospect of recruiting him. That said, Cook has the support of one high-profile observer: President Trump posted on Truth Social Thursday that Cook should replace Huang. Kurian would offer a connection to Nvidia’s AI infrastructure business. Before taking over Google Cloud in 2019, Kurian spent 22 years at Oracle , ultimately becoming president of product development. At Google Cloud, he has also worked closely with Nvidia through the companies’ AI infrastructure partnership. The question is how readily that experience would translate to leading the chipmaker itself. Arora would bring the experience of a sitting public-company chief executive with a career spanning enterprise technology, global sales and investment. Before joining the cybersecurity company in 2018, Arora was president and COO of SoftBank and held senior commercial roles at Google, including chief business officer. His appeal as a candidate could depend on whether Nvidia wants a strategist who can build around its technical leaders. There may be pros and cons for each potential candidate, but the board’s choice will ultimately determine Nvidia’s fate. “There’s such a small pool to fish in when you think about people capable of stepping into this,” Simmons said.

sources.title: NVIDIA podría destituir a Jensen Huang como CEO tras el escándalo con la espía china
sources.text: Jensen Huang podría perder su puesto como director ejecutivo de NVIDIA . De acuerdo con The Wall Street Journal , la junta directiva estaría preparando una reunión para decidir el futuro del fundador y CEO de la compañía. Las cosas se complicaron para Huang luego de que una investigación interna descubriera vínculos con una supuesta espía china. Según el reporte, el consejo de administración considera destituir a Huang después de que salieran a la luz dos relaciones extramaritales . Hace unos días, el CEO reconoció que había sido infiel a su esposa y pidió disculpas por traicionar la confianza de su familia y de la organización. La figura en el centro de esa polémica es Alice Huang, una ejecutiva de la compañía Megaspeed y con vínculos con el gobierno de Xi Jinping. Los primeros rumores apuntaban a que Megaspeed habría ayudado a desviar chips de IA hacia China . La compañía, con sede en Singapur, se convirtió en uno de los principales clientes de NVIDIA para la construcción de centros de datos de IA en el sudeste asiático. No obstante, las autoridades estadounidenses sospecharon que Huang ayudó a contrabandear tarjetas gráficas , por lo cual abrieron una investigación a finales de 2024. La relación entre Jensen Huang y Alice Huang comenzó en 2023 y permitió que la ejecutiva china desviara 240.000 placas gráficas H100, H200 y A100 hacia el gigante asiático. The Information reveló que Huang montó una red de empresas en China junto con su hermana y esposo, incluyendo una que le ayudó a convertirse en socio preferente de NVIDIA. Este movimiento le garantizó acceso prioritario a los chips y al CEO de la empresa. Hace unas semanas surgió un reporte de que Alice Huang estaba vinculada a los servicios de inteligencia chinos. El Departamento de Justicia abrió múltiples investigaciones relacionadas con ella y el mundo se le vino encima al jefe de NVIDIA. Según informó el New York Times , Alice Huang (también conocida como Huang Le) trabajaba para el Ministerio de Seguridad del Estado de China mientras mantenía una relación romántica con el directivo de la empresa de tarjetas gráficas. Los investigadores temen que pueda haber accedido a detalles técnicos sobre el hardware de IA de NVIDIA y las discusiones internas con la Casa Blanca. Hasta ahora, las autoridades se han centrado en su papel como ejecutiva de Megaspeed, donde aprovechó su cercanía con Jensen Huang para ayudar a eludir los controles de exportación estadounidenses. Además de esta relación, el New York Times señaló que el jefe de NVIDIA mantuvo un romance con otra empleada de la compañía . Kimberly Powell, vicepresidente del área de atención médica de NVIDIA, fue captada en un vídeo con Jensen Huang mientras se encontraban en un hotel de San José, California. Las políticas internas de la compañía prohíben este tipo de acciones, sobre todo cuando se trata de una relación extramarital entre un jefe y su subordinada. Hasta el momento de esta publicación, el futuro de Jensen Huang permanece en el aire . Si la junta decide apartarlo del cargo, NVIDIA perdería al hombre que transformó la compañía y la convirtió en una de las más valiosas del mundo. Huang ha sido el rostro visible de la empresa por más de tres décadas, primero en su etapa gamer y ahora en el desarrollo de chips para centros de datos, por lo que encontrar un sucesor será un trabajo complejo.

sources.title: Jensen Huang renuncia ao cargo de CEO da Nvidia após admitir traição
sources.text: Por Gabriel Cavalheiro | 12/11/2026 às 11:48 • Atualizado 12/11/2026 às 11:56 O CEO e cofundador da Nvidia, Jensen Huang, renunciou ao cargo nesta quinta-feira (12) , após admitir publicamente uma relação extraconjugal com a ex-diretora da Megaspeed International e empresária Alice Huang. A executiva é investigada por espionagem a serviço do Ministério de Segurança do Estado da China. A atual CFO da empresa, Colette Kress, foi nomeada CEO interina enquanto o conselho busca por um novo executivo para assumir o cargo. A renúncia de Huang acontece após 33 anos na liderança da Nvidia, que tem vivido um dos seus melhores momentos por liderar o boom da inteligência artificial e fornecer componentes para data centers de IA. No ano passado, a empresa foi a primeira do mundo a ultrapassar os valores de mercado de US$ 4 trilhões e US$ 5 trilhões. A relação extraconjugal entre o ex-CEO da Nvidia e Alice Huang levantou preocupações sobre a segurança nacional dos Estados Unidos e o mercado de chips de IA . No último domingo (8), o ex-chefão da companhia de chips admitiu a traição em meio a um escândalo de espionagem chinesa . "Fui infiel à minha esposa. Minhas ações a machucaram, assim como aos nossos filhos. Não há desculpa para o que fiz. Sinto muito", escreveu o então CEO. O jornal The New York Times relatou que Jensen Huang estaria envolvido em um segundo caso , desta vez com a vice-presidente de health care da Nvidia e subordinada direta do ex-CEO, Kimberly Powell , segundo cinco funcionários da companhia. As políticas internas da Nvidia orientam os funcionários a “evitar situações em que nossas ações criem conflito”, incluindo “relacionamentos pessoais”. O acúmulo de escândalos envolvendo o ex-presidente fez com que as ações da empresa caíssem 8% nesta quarta-feira (11). A companhia também perdeu US$ 1 trilhão de valor de mercado . sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns following affairs scandal
sources.text: Nvidia Corp.’s board of directors today announced the resignation of Jensen Huang, now former chief executive and president of the artificial intelligence chipmaker, amid a scandal, naming Colette Kress, current executive vice president and chief financial officer, as interim CEO. The news arrives following numerous industry reports that the board intended to replace Huang as CEO after revelations of a second extramarital relationship with an executive at Nvidia, coming mere days after he admitted to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. News initially broke over the weekend that Huang had an affair with Alice Huang , no relation, an executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed International Pte. Ltd. and an alleged Chinese spy. The Information reported on Tuesday that Alice Huang facilitated $7.5 billion in chip sales to China. According to another report, Jensen Huang also had a relationship with Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell, who serves as vice president of healthcare. The New York Times reported last month that U.S. authorities concluded Alice Huang acted as a Chinese intelligence asset. Upon revelations of the affair, the Associated Press reported that President Trump announced that the Federal Bureau of Investigation was looking into the allegations, while adding, “I think that he’ll be in good shape.” Late Wednesday, the Nvidia board met to decide whether to oust Huang and discussed a potential replacement as CEO. Huang has no obvious single successor and owns about 3.6% of Nvidia’s stock. Reportedly, the board sought counsel from an outside firm to find someone to fill the role. With the announcement, Nvidia stock was falling more than 5% in trading today, backing off an even steeper loss at the opening. Yahoo Finance calculated that Nvidia has lost more than $600 billion in market value since the previous Thursday, likely with more shocks to come. “Nvidia’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Kress. “We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead.” Kress has served as executive vice president and CFO since joining in September 2013. Her accolades include leading the company’s finance organization and working to build the company’s dominance in the AI chip industry. Before joining Nvidia, she spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco Systems Inc. and Microsoft Corp. The CFO was intimately involved with Nvidia’s widespread financing of AI compute providers, in particular its backing of not only AI leaders OpenAI Group PBC and Anthropic PBC — the latter set to go public as early as next week — but also neoclouds such as CoreWeave Inc. and Nebius Group NV. Those financings have been criticized by some as “circular,” meaning Nvidia essentially invested in customers so they could use the money to buy more of its graphics processing units. The potential successors to Huang, who had 30 direct reports, include no one obvious choice and a succession plan apparently was not in place. Candidates that some have speculated about include Arm Ltd. CEO Rene Haas, who worked at Nvidia years ago, Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, and Ian Buck, Nvidia’s vice president and general manager of hyperscale and high-performance computing and creator of its CUDA software considered the real moat for its business. “The sudden resignation of Jensen Huang is about more than succession at the world’s most important AI chipmaker,” Forrester Vice President and Group Research Director Stephanie Balaouras told SiliconANGLE in an email. “Nvidia’s leadership crisis is a stress test for the AI boom. If Nvidia stabilizes quickly under new leadership, the AI infrastructure boom will have demonstrated resilience. If its stock, financing relationships or ecosystem commitments remain under sustained pressure, that would add evidence to the fragile side of the AI bubble ledger.”” Balaouras added that “tech leaders shouldn’t overreact, but they should treat Nvidia’s CEO transition as a prompt to reassess concentration risk across their AI infrastructure, suppliers and investment plans.” Huang is best known for co-founding Nvidia in 1993 in a San Jose Denny’s and has served as its CEO since. His departure will likely send further ripples through the AI silicon and software industry. He has been deeply involved in Nvidia’s product strategy and built longstanding customer relationships, helming the company as it became the behemoth it is today. Nvidia commands roughly 80% of the data-center AI chip market, although industry estimates vary by methodology. Epoch Artificial Intelligence Inc. puts its share of AI computing power shipped at 63% in the second quarter of 2026. Other market carve-outs include custom chips built by cloud companies within the broader supply, including Google LLC’s tensor processing units at 25%, Amazon Inc.’s custom silicon at 5% and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.’s AI hardware accelerators at 4%. La dimisión de Huang supone un cambio histórico para NVIDIA, empresa que cofundó en 1993 y que ha dirigido durante más de tres décadas. Bajo su liderazgo, la multinacional ha pasado de ser uno de los principales fabricantes de tarjetas gráficas para videojuegos a convertirse en una pieza fundamental de la industria tecnológica gracias a sus procesadores para IA . También han trascendido varios rumores sobre una posible segunda relación con Kimberly Powell, una directiva de NVIDIA que trabajaba bajo su supervisión. Kress mantendrá también sus responsabilidades económicas mientras el consejo de administración busca un sustituto permanente. Antes de incorporarse a NVIDIA, la directiva acumuló cerca de 25 años de experiencia en departamentos financieros de grandes tecnológicas , entre ellas Cisco y Microsoft. El consejo considera que su experiencia de las cuentas, así como del funcionamiento interno de la compañía la convierten en una figura relevante para garantizar la continuidad del negocio durante esta transición. Jones lleva formando parte del consejo desde 1993 y cuenta con una larga trayectoria en el sector tecnológico y de la inversión. La dimisión de Jensen Huang llega en un momento especialmente delicado para el fabricante de chips . Su figura ha sido fundamental para construir la identidad de la compañía y establecer relaciones estratégicas con los principales proveedores de servicios en la nube, desarrolladores de inteligencia artificial y fabricantes de hardware. Además, el directivo había defendido públicamente la necesidad de mantener el acceso de NVIDIA al mercado chino , incluso en un contexto de restricciones estadounidenses a la exportación de semiconductores avanzados. Su salida también introduce incertidumbre sobre la posición que adoptará la compañía en este terreno. El consejo de administración de la compañía ha transmitido un mensaje de continuidad y confianza en el equipo directivo. La empresa asegura que sus operaciones y sus compromisos con los clientes no se verán afectados.

sources.text: Nvidia ha perdido al único director ejecutivo que ha tenido jamás. Jensen Huang ha dimitido este jueves como presidente, director ejecutivo y miembro del consejo de administración, y la empresa ahora tiene que encontrar a alguien para dirigir al fabricante de chips más valioso del mundo. Por el momento, el puesto pertenece a alguien de la casa. Qué ha pasado. También ha nombrado a Harvey C. Jones, antiguo director ejecutivo de Synopsys, como presidente del consejo, siendo de hecho el primero en la historia de la empresa. La salida de Huang se produce tras las investigaciones sobre sus relaciones extramatrimoniales, una de ellas presuntamente con Alice Huang , ejecutiva y directora de la empresa Megaspeed, sospechosa de ser espía china . Las acciones de Nvidia abrieron este jueves con una caída de más del 13 % tras la dimisión, borrando más de medio billón de dólares en valor. La nueva CEO interina : Colette Kress. Ha sido directora financiera desde 2013, trabajó anteriormente en Cisco y Microsoft, y aparece junto a Huang en cada presentación de resultados. Josh Gilbert, analista de eToro, declaraba a Reuters que es “la opción obvia para mantener el rumbo” y una voz de confianza para los inversores. Ahora, que se quede de forma permanente es otra cosa. Para Gilbert la ventaja de Nvidia es la tecnología y el consejo probablemente querría a un ingeniero al mando. Los ingenieros. Ian Buck, quien ayudó a desarrollar CUDA, el software que mantiene a los desarrolladores vinculados a los chips de Nvidia, y que ahora dirige los productos de IA a hiperescala, encabeza la lista para llevarse el puesto permanente. Los externos. Armina Rosenberg, de Minotaur Capital, ve plausible también una estructura de codirección ejecutiva, combinando a un líder financiero como Kress con un líder tecnológico como Buck. Qué pasa ahora. De momento, y hasta conocer más noticias, tendremos que esperar al próximo martes 17 de noviembre, que es cuando Nvidia presenta sus resultados del tercer trimestre bajo el mando de Kress. sources.title: Trump pide a Tim Cook como CEO de NVIDIA tras la renuncia de Jensen Huang: «Una leyenda por otra leyenda»
sources.text: La renuncia de Jensen Huang como CEO de NVIDIA es, sin dudas, el tema del día . El escándalo por infidelidades le ha costado al empresario el puesto que ostentó durante los últimos 33 años , y el asunto promete seguir dando que hablar por bastante tiempo. Lo más curioso es que todos tienen una opinión sobre el tema y hasta Donald Trump ha propuesto a un reemplazante de alto perfil: Tim Cook . En las horas posteriores a la salida de Jensen Huang, Trump usó su perfil en Truth Social para postular a Cook como próximo CEO de NVIDIA. De acuerdo con el presidente de Estados Unidos, el exCEO de Apple es la única persona que tiene lo necesario para hacerse cargo de un rol tan complejo. A sabiendas de cómo piensa y actúa Donald Trump, no quedan dudas de que el mandatario estadounidense habla en serio. Claro que hoy parece improbable que Tim Cook esté dispuesto a asumir un rol tan notorio fuera de Apple, en especial por lo repentino y desastroso del desenlace de Jensen Huang. "Ahora que el CEO de NVIDIA, Jensen Huang, quien ha hecho un trabajo fantástico, ha renunciado, solo hay un hombre capaz de tomar su lugar: Tim Cook, de Apple. ¡Una leyenda reemplaza a otra leyenda! Presidente Donald J. Trump", publicó el presidente de Estados Unidos. Más allá de las virtudes de Jensen Huang y Tim Cook para conducir durante gran cantidad de años (y con gran éxito) a sus respectivas empresas, Trump no ofrece detalles de por qué el exjefe de Apple debería reemplazar a su antiguo colega en NVIDIA. Tal vez solo sea porque Cook ha sabido congraciarse con el presidente estadounidense durante sus mandatos, tal y como lo hizo Huang en su momento. Sea como sea, todavía no se sabe quién reemplazará definitivamente a Jensen Huang. Colette Kress , la jefa de finanzas de NVIDIA, fungirá de CEO interina hasta que se designe a un nuevo responsable del cargo. La junta del gigante verde anunció la puesta en marcha de un proceso de búsqueda de nuevo consejero delegado, para la cual analizará a candidatos internos y externos. Asimismo, se ha designado a Harvey C. Jones como presidente del board , el primero en ocupar ese rol en la historia de la compañía. ¿Tiene posibilidades Tim Cook de ser el próximo CEO de NVIDIA? Hasta hace menos de 15 días, era inaudito pensar en dicha empresa sin Jensen Huang como jefe, pero ya hemos visto que los imposibles no existen y que no se puede descartar nada. Dicho esto, Cook se encuentra extremadamente cómodo en su nuevo rol como presidente ejecutivo de Apple. Además, no es un directivo enfocado en producto como sí lo fue Jensen Huang ; algo que podría no importar en cualquier otra empresa, pero que ha sido crucial para el crecimiento de NVIDIA bajo el comando de un único CEO en sus 33 años de vida. Ya veremos qué novedades surgen en tal sentido.

sources.title: Ex-NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang is set to testify before Congress this month
sources.text: House Foreign Affairs Chair Brian Mast said the hearing will take place before Thanksgiving. Jensen Huang might have stepped down from his roles at the top of NVIDIA, but he won't be sliding out of the spotlight just yet. The company's former CEO and president is set to testify before Congress by Thanksgiving, according to House representatives. House Foreign Affairs Chairman Brian Mast said Huang agreed to testify on Wednesday — hours before NVIDIA announced his resignation with immediate effect — after lawmakers threatened him with a subpoena. It appears the hearing will take place behind closed doors (which is unfortunate, because that's likely to be some spicy testimony). However, Mast expects it to be filmed and transcribed, according to Bloomberg . The House's Intelligence and China-focused committees will join the Foreign Affairs cohort for the hearing. "Jensen and I have been very at odds as some of you already know on export controls, but NVIDIA is a very important company to the United States of America," Mast said. "I don't want to see anything hurt in NVIDIA, but he has some very serious questions to answer." NVIDIA has been in turmoil after it emerged over the weekend that the company was investigating Huang over an affair to which he admitted, allegedly with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. President Donald Trump said the FBI is investigating the situation as well. On Wednesday, it was reported that Huang had another affair, this time with Kimberly Powell, an NVIDIA executive who reported to him. The company's board met later that day to determine Huang's future. Colette Kress, NVIDIA's executive vice president and chief financial officer, is stepping in as interim CEO while the company seeks a permanent successor. Meanwhile, the Department of Justice is reportedly investigating Alice Huang , the alleged spy, to determine whether entities associated with her were involved in attempts to smuggle Super Micro Computer products to China. The DoJ is also said to be taking the lead in an investigation into her former company, the Singapore-based Megaspeed International, over alleged smuggling of US-made chips into China in defiance of export restrictions. The company said it would cooperate with the probe . Officials in Singapore opened an investigation into Alice Huang, Megaspeed and associated individuals last year. The Ministry of Home Affairs said in a statement on Thursday that she was barred from re-entering the country after police determined she knowingly offered up inaccurate information to downplay her role in Megaspeed. However, they "concluded that there was insufficient evidence to establish that Huang had committed any offences relating to the possible inaccurate declarations for which Megaspeed was being investigated." The investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals is ongoing.

Embora o código de conduta da NVIDIA não proíba expressamente todos os relacionamentos entre gestores e subordinados, as normas internas exigem que potenciais conflitos de interesse sejam reportados ao departamento jurídico. Além disso, trata-se de uma quebra de aliança matrimonial. Para conduzir a apuração independente, o conselho contratou o escritório de advocacia Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. Caso a demissão de Huang se confirme, a empresa enfrentará um vácuo inédito de liderança: como o executivo mantém uma estrutura administrativa horizontal onde dezenas de vice-presidentes respondem diretamente a ele, não há um sucessor natural óbvio. Enquanto isso, os trabalhos dentro da gigante seguem, já que os data centers não podem parar. Para os gamers, tem sobrado cada vez menos. Parceiras da NVIDIA já até afirmaram que a empresa tem interrompido o fornecimento de chips para a fabricação de placas de vídeo GeForce RTX .

Apesar do sobrenome em comum, ela não tem parentesco com Jensen Huang. As ações da Nvidia desabaram mais de 24% em 30 dias. A empresa perdeu US$ 1,081 trilhão (cerca de R$ 6,1 trilhões) em valor de mercado entre 29 de outubro e 10 de novembro, segundo levantamento da Elos Ayta. No domingo (8), a companhia abriu uma investigação independente para apurar se ele foi alvo de uma operação de inteligência de outro país. Nesta quarta (11), o jornal New York Times revelou que Jensen também teve outro caso extraconjugal, desta vez com Kimberly Powell, vice-presidente da área de saúde da Nvidia. Em comunicado, a Nvidia informou que Colette Kress, atual vice-presidente executiva e diretora financeira, assumirá temporariamente o comando da empresa. Segundo a empresa, Kress teve um papel fundamental no crescimento da Nvidia à frente da área financeira. Comunicado da Nvidia sobre afastamento de Jensen Huang “O Conselho de Administração da NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) anunciou hoje que Jensen Huang renunciou aos cargos de Presidente, Diretor Executivo e membro do Conselho, com efeito imediato. Jones como seu primeiro Presidente do Conselho. sources.title: Saída de Jensen Huang abala Nvidia e pode redefinir o futuro da inteligência
sources.text: A renúncia de Jensen Huang ao comando da Nvidia abre uma incerteza que vai além da sucessão na fabricante de chips: a continuidade das relações comerciais e financeiras que ajudam a sustentar a expansão da inteligência artificial. O executivo tinha papel central na articulação de investimentos entre empresas do setor. A mudança ocorre em um momento em que fabricantes de semicondutores , provedores de nuvem e desenvolvedores de IA dependem de grandes compromissos financeiros para ampliar a infraestrutura necessária ao treinamento e à operação de modelos. A influência da Nvidia no mercado não se limita à venda de processadores. A empresa também participa de um ecossistema de investimentos e acordos com companhias que precisam de capacidade computacional para desenvolver serviços de inteligência artificial . Nesse arranjo, provedores de nuvem e laboratórios de IA dependem de infraestrutura equipada com chips da fabricante, enquanto os investimentos e compromissos comerciais ajudam a viabilizar novas instalações. Huang teve participação direta na construção dessas relações. Sua atuação envolvia não apenas a estratégia tecnológica da Nvidia, mas também a articulação com parceiros e clientes que impulsionam a demanda por seus produtos. A saída do executivo, portanto, levanta dúvidas sobre a capacidade da companhia de manter esse ritmo de coordenação. O desafio não está necessariamente no desenvolvimento dos próximos chips . A Nvidia conta com equipes técnicas e um planejamento de produtos que não dependem exclusivamente de seu fundador. A questão é como a empresa manterá a rede de acordos, investimentos e operações que conecta diferentes participantes do mercado de IA. Um dos pontos de atenção é o chamado financiamento circular. O modelo ocorre quando empresas que fornecem tecnologia ou infraestrutura também investem em clientes ou oferecem garantias que ajudam a financiar compras de seus próprios produtos e serviços. Esse tipo de relação pode acelerar a construção de data centers e a expansão da capacidade computacional. Ao mesmo tempo, cria vínculos financeiros entre empresas que dependem umas das outras para manter seus planos de crescimento. Se compromissos forem revistos ou novos investimentos demorarem a sair, os efeitos podem alcançar diferentes partes da cadeia. Anúncios e acordos envolvendo empresas como OpenAI , CoreWeave e Anthropic ilustram a dimensão dos recursos mobilizados para ampliar a infraestrutura de inteligência artificial. A continuidade desses projetos depende de financiamento, disponibilidade de equipamentos e confiança na demanda futura. A renúncia de Huang não significa que esses compromissos serão interrompidos. Mas sua saída acrescenta uma variável à avaliação dos investidores: quem assumirá a articulação de negócios em um setor no qual decisões de investimento de uma empresa podem influenciar os planos de várias outras? A reação inicial das ações mostrou a dimensão da preocupação dos investidores. Os papéis da Nvidia recuaram mais de 12% nas negociações iniciais desta quinta-feira (12), movimento que poderia retirar cerca de US$ 500 bilhões (aproximadamente R$ 2,78 trilhões) de seu valor de mercado. AMD e Broadcom, por outro lado, registraram altas de 2% e 5%, respectivamente. A diretora financeira Colette Kress assumirá o comando interinamente, enquanto a empresa avalia candidatos internos e externos para a sucessão definitiva. A Nvidia também terá de demonstrar que consegue preservar sua estratégia comercial e os relacionamentos construídos por Huang. O desempenho financeiro recente oferece uma base operacional robusta: a companhia reportou US$ 96,2 bilhões (cerca de R$ 533,9 bilhões) em receita no último trimestre. Ainda assim, os próximos resultados, previstos para 17 de novembro, serão acompanhados não apenas pelos números de vendas, mas também por sinais sobre demanda, entregas e novos investimentos. O alcance da transição será medido, portanto, pela capacidade da Nvidia de manter sua posição na cadeia de infraestrutura da IA. Mais do que encontrar um novo CEO, a empresa precisa mostrar que o ecossistema de negócios construído durante a gestão de Huang pode continuar funcionando sem depender de sua presença direta. Valdir Antonelli é jornalista com especialização em marketing digital e consumo.

sources.title: A divisão gamer da Nvidia pode acabar? O que acontecerá com a GeForce após renúncia de Jensen Huang
sources.text: O dia 12 de novembro de 2026 ficará marcado no mundo da tecnologia como um dos mais improváveis e até mesmo mais importantes de sua história. Nesta quinta-feira, Jensen Huang, o CEO e cofundador da Nvidia, renunciou ao cargo após um escândalo de adultério e espionagem. As reações do mercado de tecnologia e Wall Street já eram esperadas. Somente nas últimas horas, as ações da companhia verde caíram mais de 13%. O próprio Huang saiu do seleto grupo das dez pessoas mais ricas do mundo nos últimos três dias ao perder quase US$ 10 bilhões (cerca de R$ 50 bilhões) de sua fortuna absurda, estimada em mais de R$ 700 bilhões. Por mais que a indústria de tecnologia e o segmento de IA possam enfrentar um período de incertezas, a expectativa é que esse mercado continue firme. No entanto, a pergunta que uma generosa parcela do público começa a fazer é: o que acontece com os gamers de computador? Além do gigantismo em IA, a Nvidia é dona da tradicional linha de placas de vídeo GeForce, que alimenta 72% dos computadores dos gamers, segundo dados da Steam. Jogar no PC e usar uma Nvidia GeForce se tornou basicamente um sinônimo para muitos, e agora impera o medo de que essa divisão esteja ameaçada. A Nvidia publicou uma nota recente que explica a renúncia de Jensen Huang como diretor da empresa. Interinamente, Colette Kress atuará como CEO da companhia até que a empresa e o Conselho encontrem um executivo (a) definitivo. Em outras palavras, as portas da Nvidia estão abertas e não há como prever integralmente quais mudanças serão implementadas na gigante. Mesmo assim, a curto e até médio prazo talvez seja seguro dizer que a divisão GeForce de placas de vídeo ficará intocada. É verdade que a Nvidia já direcionava seus esforços quase que totalmente para o segmento corporativo, mas isso não quer dizer que a empresa abandonará seu braço de gráficos e GPUs. Arthur Igreja, especialista em tecnologia e inovação, aponta que o estágio embrionário do momento impossibilita fazer previsões assertivas . No entanto, ele explica que é improvável a Nvidia simplesmente se livrar da linha gamer, afinal de contas, ninguém parece disposto a se livrar de uma divisão inteira assim. Uma coisa é ter foco, outra, completamente diferente, é abrir mão. Essa ainda é uma linha de receita importante para a Nvidia. O especialista salienta que em momentos de crise, como o atual, a companhia precisará reunir todas as suas linhas para maximizar o lucro. O fato de a divisão GeForce existir pode até mesmo ser um fator positivo para a companhia. Aliás, a nova CEO era diretora financeira da empresa, então ela deve saber da importância dessa série e pode evitar cortes desnecessários agora. Claro, isso não significa que os produtos GeForce ficarão intocados para sempre . Um futuro CEO pode entender que a linha gamer e de itens domésticos não faz sentido e focar toda a infraestrutura da empresa para o setor corporativo. Mesmo assim, isso seria um movimento brusco extremamente arriscado. Vale notar que o mundo do hardware doméstico contempla apenas três empresas: Nvidia, AMD e Intel. A AMD é a única com força para produzir amplamente CPUs e GPUs, e a Intel engatinha no cenário das placas de vídeo. Abrir mão da série GeForce seria entregar o mercado de bandeja para a AMD e ver a Intel ganhar terreno ao longo dos anos. Arthur Igreja também aponta que o movimento de saída de Jensen Huang da Nvidia também não deve ser motivo para reduzir a crise de componentes global. “A questão da demanda é um fator externo, exógeno. Ela depende muito mais das hyperscalers e do restante do mercado, além de fatores como um eventual aumento da regulação [...] Em última instância, a NVIDIA continua sendo uma fornecedora. Ela não representa o mercado como um todo e não controla a demanda”. Mesmo com sua atuação distante do segmento gamer, Colette Kress já mostrou em algumas oportunidades que entende o fenômeno. Durante uma conversa com analistas da JPMorgan na CES 2026, a executiva foi questionada sobre a ausência de novidades para o setor na feira e respondeu que “o negócio de games tem sido um sucesso estrondoso”. Aliás, a própria entrada de Kress na Nvidia em 2013 aconteceu por conta do setor de games. Ela entrou na companhia após seus filhos recomendarem a marca por conta dos bons produtos gamer que produzia. O TecMundo já possui um ótimo conteúdo que conta detalhadamente a história completa da Nvidia, mas é sempre bom relembrar como um gigante se ergue. Tudo começou em 1993, quando Curtis Priem, Christopher Malachowski e um jovem chamado Jensen Huang fundaram a Nvidia em Sunnyvale, na Califórnia. Engana-se quem pensa que a estrada até o sucesso da Nvidia foi pavimentada com ouro - ou melhor, silício. O primeiro chip comercial da companhia surgiu apenas em 1995, o NV1, mas foi em 1997 que as coisas realmente começaram a engrenar graças ao sucesso da linha Riva. Mas foi em outubro de 1999 que a linha GeForce deu seu passo inaugural com a GeForce 256. Jensen e seus amigos acreditavam que os computadores se tornaram uma plataforma multimídia e de jogos 3D. A chegada da GeForce 256 confirmou isso ao se tornar a primeira GPU como conhecemos hoje. De 1999 até 2026 tem muita história para contar. A Nvidia comprou rivais, como a 3dfx, desenvolveu o chip do primeiro Xbox, do PlayStation 3, fez com que os usuários pudessem usar várias placas de vídeo em um único PC e por aí vai. Lá em 2008 a companhia verde resolveu lançar uma placa chamada GTX 280. A partir de então, as GTX se tornaram as placas de vídeo definitivas para os jogadores, mesmo a rival AMD tendo adquirido a fabricante de GPUs ATI para rivalizar forças. Não tinha jeito, a Nvidia dominava esse segmento. Os anos passaram e uma década depois da introdução da GTX 280 a Nvidia resolveu revolucionar o mundo dos PCs de novo: entrou em cena a linha RTX. Esses produtos, que perduram até hoje, tinham o poder para calcular raios de luz em tempo real, o Ray Tracing, e isso possibilitou que os games ficassem exponencialmente

sources.text: In today’s newsletter: US intelligence reportedly believes the former tech executive was recruited by Beijing, raising questions about the security of the AI industry and Trump’s close ties to Nvidia chief Jensen Huang Good morning. Espionage is supposed to be a secretive business, and spies are supposed to be virtually invisible. That hasn’t been the case for Alice Huang, the mysterious Shanghai executive who formed a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang , the founder of Nvidia, one of America’s most powerful tech companies. Many questions have arisen since it emerged that US intelligence believes that Huang (no relation of Jensen’s) is an asset recruited by the Chinese intelligence services to spy on behalf of Beijing. This morning’s newsletter explains what we know about the story, and what it tells us about the effectiveness of Chinese espionage. That’s after the headlines. UK | Ministers are considering changing the law to force the entertainment industry to better protect women and children in the wake of the revelations over David Walliams and the conviction of Russell Brand. Climate | The UK government has appointed the world’s first special representative for climate security, in the strongest sign yet of fears that climate breakdown will bring chaos to the country. US midterms | Democrat Scott Colom has become the first Black senator in Mississippi to be elected since Reconstruction, in a stunning upset after more than a week of vote counting in one of the country’s most reliably red states. Europe | Millions of people across Spain have joined the country’s first general strike in 14 years , setting up picket lines to protest against soaring housing prices before an election in which the far right could be catapulted into power. Technology | Police officers risk arresting innocent people , especially from ethnic minorities, if they treat inaccurate facial recognition data as evidence, an official report has found. Last month, the New York Times reported that Jensen Huang had formed a “close relationship” with Alice Huang, the former executive of a Singapore-based computing company, Megaspeed. Megaspeed is a customer of Nvidia; it buys the extremely valuable chips they produce, which are essential for powering AI, and rents computing space to Chinese companies. The US government had already been investigating whether Megaspeed could be flouting US restrictions and smuggling chips into China – allegations that both Nvidia and Megaspeed deny. US intelligence officials, who had been conducting surveillance on Alice Huang, eventually concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset who had been passing on information to Beijing. The intelligence behind this assessment is classified, so we don’t know exactly what they found – or which intelligence body was conducting the surveillance. Nvidia said Jensen Huang’s interactions with Alice Huang were “not unusual or unexpected”, but on Sunday, Huang admitted in a letter to his employees that he had been having an affair. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children,” he said, adding that he was “deeply sorry”. Nvidia’s valuation is inextricably linked to Huang. By yesterday, $430bn (5.5%) had been wiped off its share price, and in the early hours of this morning, that figure ballooned to about $600bn following reports that Nvidia’s board was deciding whether to oust Huang (you can follow the latest on that here ). The company has appointed outside counsel to review the pair’s relationship and says it has no reason to believe that secrets or national security were compromised. The most interesting aspects of this story are the questions we can’t (yet) answer. Did Nvidia’s board know that US intelligence suspected Alice Huang was a spy? What evidence led US intelligence to conclude she was spying for China ? What information could she have passed to Beijing? And … Reporters and sleuths on Chinese social media have been trying to get to the bottom of who the Megaspeed chief really is. On Tuesday, the Financial Times published an interesting report (£) about Alice Huang’s backstory. She was born in the rural area of Hunan, worked as a journalist at China’s state broadcaster, then at HSBC and the investment bank Citic Securities. In 2015, she joined an investment management company Hexi. There, she met financier Kang Wei. The two became romantically involved, and together they reinvented themselves as AI entrepreneurs. In 2023, Huang and her business partners acquired Megaspeed, a Singaporean subsidiary of a Chinese gaming company, which she and Wei aimed to turn into a datacentre business. According to the FT’s report, the two pitched investors on their ability to secure access to Nvidia chips. Nobody knows exactly when Jensen Huang met Alice Huang, when their relationship became romantic, or what information she might have passed to Beijing while it was going on. The earliest picture of them together is at an after-party following a tech trade show in Taipei, taken in 2024. As Aisha Down and Dan Milmo pointed out earlier this week, Jensen Huang is close to Donald Trump, so it’s possible that Alice Huang could have gained glimpses into US AI policy as it was being formed, into Trump’s thinking on AI, or into Nvidia’s company strategy. But without seeing the evidence, all this is speculation. What does this reveal about Chinese espionage? The US has been historically cautious about allowing AI chips to end up in Chinese hands. In 2022, Joe Biden’s administration introduced the Chips and Science Act, which restricted the sale of US chips in China, banning the export of most Nvidia chips. “The Chinese have a very strong pedigree for industrial espionage and copying other nations’ technologies,” Steve Tsang, the director of the SOAS China Institute, tells me. “They’ve been doing this for decades. sources.title: Before Megaspeed, there was Supermicro: The other Nvidia partner tied to China chip smuggling—and to Jensen Huang
sources.text: Whether she was a spy, a fixer, or just a paramour of Jensen Huang, the name Alice Huang (no relation) has roiled the business world this week following reports that the two were having an affair. The revelation snowballed into Jensen’s shocking resignation Wednesday. Now come reports that officials are looking into other companies Alice was working with. Bloomberg reported , based on an anonymous source, that the Department of Justice is running multiple probes into Nvidia . One is focused on antitrust issues and two others are focused on Megaspeed—where Alice Huang was a former top executive—and Super Micro Computer . Separately, the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Manhattan is probing whether entities linked to Alice Huang were involved in alleged efforts to smuggle Supermicro hardware laced with Nvidia’s red-hot GPUs into China. It is unclear whether that probe is tied to smuggling cases already brought in the U.S. or Asia. Neither Jensen Huang, Nvidia, nor Supermicro have been formally charged with any wrongdoing. Supermicro stock tumbled 12% after U.S. markets opened this morning. The company did not immediately respond to Fortune ’s request for comment. Thus far, much of the speculation about Jensen Huang’s catastrophic downfall as the leader of Nvidia has centered on Megaspeed, the Singapore firm that reportedly became one of Nvidia’s largest buyers in Southeast Asia. But Supermicro, the San Jose server maker run by Charles Liang, Jensen Huang’s friend of three decades and an important partner to Nvidia, has been in under the microscope regarding export-control compliance and is being pulled along with Nvidia. Fortune has reported on the Supermicro case since before federal agents arrested its co-founder in March, and that reporting shows a company with a documented track record of governance and compliance failures. Despite its history, Supermicro has remained in lockstep with Nvidia. Liang and Jensen have shared the stage together at Computex in Taiwan, where Jensen was photographed in 2024 with Alice at a cocktail bar. In March, federal prosecutors charged Supermicro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw and two others with allegedly routing about $2.5 billion in servers laced with Nvidia H200 and B200 GPUs to China through a Southeast Asian front company. Bloomberg later reported the front company is OBON, a Bangkok-based AI infrastructure firm, which has not been charged. Supermicro was not charged and has said it was a victim of the scheme. Liaw, who immediately resigned his executive and board roles at Supermicro following his arrest, has pleaded not guilty. His trial was pushed to March 2027 after Liaw’s lawyers told the judge in his case that subpoenas issued to Supermicro could be material to Liaw’s defense. Nelson Boxer, Liaw’s attorney, declined to comment. One of Liaw’s co-defendants in the smuggling case, Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun, pleaded guilty in October, including to a charge that he deleted an encrypted messaging app from his phone on the day of the arrests. Sun’s attorneys did not respond to a request for comment, and it’s unclear if Sun has a cooperation agreement with the government. There is no public evidence so far that the Supermicro and Megaspeed cases are directly connected but there are mounting threads. Thursday, Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs issued a statement noting that the Singapore Police Force and Customs had initiated investigations into Megaspeed and Alice Huang and in doing so sought information from Supermicro. Supermicro only offered “limited cooperation,” Singaporean authorities said. In a July 2025 meeting, Singapore officials raised this with U.S. authorities and asked for their assistance in getting Supermicro’s cooperation and have repeated the request “on several occasions” to the Department of Justice and the FBI. “Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company,” the statement reads. Supermicro did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Supermicro’s export-control problems did not start with Liaw’s arrest, Fortune ’s reporting has found. In 2006, the company pleaded guilty to illegally exporting computer equipment to Iran through a distributor in Dubai, mirroring the basic scheme prosecutors alleged in the Liaw case. Liaw himself has been through the crisis wringer before. He left Supermicro in 2018 amid a board-led investigation tied to Supermicro’s Nasdaq delisting and an SEC probe of its accounting, which ended with a $17.5 million settlement in 2020. Liaw returned as a consultant in May 2021, became a full-time employee, and rejoined the board in December 2023. In 2024, short seller Hindenburg Research accused Supermicro of accounting manipulation and export-control failures and the company denied the allegations. Ernst & Young then resigned as auditor mid-audit, saying it could no longer rely on management’s representations. A special committee recommended in December 2024 that Supermicro replace CFO David Weigand and the company agreed to do so “immediately .” The company didn’t name a successor until October. As Fortune has reported, the Liaw indictment describes thousands of nonworking dummy servers staged in warehouses to fool auditors, contractors using hair dryers to peel off serial-number labels, and a compliance auditor who was off-site allegedly enjoying “entertainment” paid for by another company during an inspection. It also shows how the alleged scheme fed directly into Nvidia’s supply pipeline. In December 2024, Liaw allegedly told the front company that “the only way” to get Nvidia to commit B200 chip allocations was to create monthly forecasts. Nvidia is not accused of wrongdoing in the Liaw indictment. sources.title: Alice Huang tied to Nvidia’s biggest Chinese competitor
sources.text: Alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang may have owned stakes in businesses in China that benefited Nvidia's biggest competitor in China, Huawei, at the same time that she was in business with Nvidia and also reportedly having a romantic affair with its ousted CEO Jensen Huang . The connection between Alice Huang and Huawei was first discovered by analysts at private intelligence firm Tesari. The firm exclusively shared its findings with CNBC. Tesari, which uses artificial intelligence to collect evidence and specializes in national security investigations around the world, provides intelligence research to private companies and the U.S. government. This previously unreported entanglement may raise questions about Alice Huang's intent and conduct in her relationship with the CEO and whether Jensen Huang knew his romantic partner was closely connected with his competition. Jensen Huang has acknowledged having an affair, though the precise timing of his relationship with Alice Huang is unknown. The mysterious saga of Alice Huang involves a tangle of interlocking corporations and transactions that show her connection to entities that ultimately provided computing power to Huawei in China.
